findings.title: total_connections leaked when shard-aware connection lands on full shard
findings.claim: A shard-aware connection landing on an already-full shard is dropped after inc_total_connections() charged it at :1051, with nothing decrementing it; reviewer reproduced the gauge drifting to 2 while the pool holds 1. The 'probably due to NAT' comment shows this is not a rare path, so the gauge drifts up unbounded.

findings.title: Unconditional current_keyspace set bricks pool when USE keyspace keeps failing
findings.claim: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace sets current_keyspace unconditionally before USE is attempted, and with discard-on-failure every new connection is rejected as long as USE keeps failing, draining pools, publishing Broken(UseKeyspaceError), and killing the session for all queries including fully-qualified ones; pre-PR this degraded gracefully, and the larger blast radius is undocumented.

findings.title: USE-failure log downgraded from warn! to debug! exactly when it became consequential
findings.claim: Old code warned while keeping the connection; new code debugs while discarding it, and with a non-empty pool update_shared_conns isn't called, so nothing surfaces the error at default levels and the pool silently stops growing.

findings.title: No Drop on PoolRefiller leaks the whole connection count on pool teardown
findings.claim: Tearing a pool down leaks its whole count because there's no Drop on PoolRefiller; this is pre-existing and a test actually depends on this behavior.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loop can wrap AtomicU64 on over-decrement
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections loops N fetch_sub(1) calls against a raw AtomicU64 fetch_sub with no saturation, so one over-decrement wraps to ~1.8e19; a saturating sub_total_connections(n) would fail safe.

findings.title: ConnectionSetupError is undocumented and name-collides with public ConnectionSetupRequestError
findings.claim: ConnectionSetupError is undocumented and name-collides with the public errors::ConnectionSetupRequestError, which it also contains.

findings.title: Commit messages are subject-only, violating CONTRIBUTING.md's what-and-why requirement
findings.claim: All four commits are subject-only even though CONTRIBUTING.md:10 requires what and why and repo history follows it; the PR checklist claims otherwise.

findings.title: Fixup commit 617139df should be squashed into 0d91aa54
findings.claim: 617139df is a fixup to 0d91aa54 and should be squashed.

findings.title: Two keyspace tests skip setup_tracing() unlike every other test in the module
findings.claim: The two keyspace tests at :1474 and :1526 skip setup_tracing(), unlike every other test in the module.

findings.title: PR Validation section's cargo test line inaccurately implies metrics tests were run
findings.claim: The three metrics tests are behind the non-default metrics feature, so the quoted cargo test line never compiled them; they do run in CI's --all-features, so this is an accuracy issue in the PR description, not a coverage gap.

findings.title: Reorder drops sharder/shard-aware-port learning on the USE-failure path without a comment
findings.claim: The reorder at :874-893 drops sharder / shard-aware-port learning on the USE-failure path; a test asserts this so it reads intentional, but it needs a one-line comment at the early return.

findings.title: "Avoid busy-waiting" fix is still a 1ms poll loop reliant on select! branch ordering
findings.claim: The avoid-busy-waiting fix at :1993-2000 is still a 1ms poll loop, and leans on select! picking the initial scheduled_refill branch with zero opens.

findings.title: make_rules re-implements start_simulated_node's OPTIONS/STARTUP rules instead of parameterizing it
findings.claim: make_rules at :1527-1566 re-implements start_simulated_node's OPTIONS/STARTUP rules instead of parameterizing the existing function.

findings.title: New ConnectionError variant checked for semver break — none found
findings.claim: #[non_exhaustive] was already on ConnectionError, so the new variant is not a semver break.

findings.title: Checked for new clippy warnings vs base — none found
findings.claim: No new clippy warnings vs base, including no new result_large_err.

findings.title: Checked conns-sizing invariant around maybe_reshard — holds
findings.claim: maybe_reshard still runs before conns[shard_id] is indexed, so the conns-sizing invariant holds.

findings.title: Checked remove_connection for double-decrement — cannot happen
findings.claim: remove_connection can't double-decrement because of Arc::ptr_eq against already-cleared vectors.

findings.title: Checked keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state test authenticity — genuine
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state is a genuine regression test against a real proxy node, not a mock.

findings.title: -Dwarnings result_large_err expectation error set aside as pre-existing
findings.claim: The -Dwarnings result_large_err expectation error in cc_establisher.rs:251 reproduces at base and was set aside as pre-existing/unrelated.

findings.title: many_connections test failure set aside as needing a live SCYLLA_URI
findings.claim: The many_connections failure needs a live SCYLLA_URI and was set aside as pre-existing/unrelated.

findings.title: Missing USE timeout set aside as pre-existing TODO, though PR enlarges its blast radius
findings.claim: The missing USE timeout at :1336 is a pre-existing TODO set aside as pre-existing/unrelated, though this PR enlarges its blast radius.

findings.title: Stale shared_conns window in maybe_reshard set aside as pre-existing/unrelated
findings.claim: The stale shared_conns window in maybe_reshard was set aside as pre-existing/unrelated.
